Attention from response tokens to the question fades sharply later in these two answers, most strongly for heads L17h0 (0.38 to 0.04), L17h2 (0.34 to 0.03) and L11h1 (0.28 to 0.06). This is weak evidence, though: both texts are loops, where attention naturally moves to the previous copy, and attention mass is diluted as the context grows.

A sharper and more relevant question is which full-attention heads fetch an operand from the question at the moment the model writes it. That is the step the reference logprobs show to be weak (operand starts at -0.69) and the step behind errors like treating a rate as a total. I'll spend one teacher-forced pass on the original model over two reference solutions, with prompt, that copy several numbers from the question, and save attention for layers 5, 11, 17 and 23. A head that, at operand tokens, attends strongly to the matching number in the question would be a number-fetching head and a candidate for a causal test: ablating it should lower operand logprobs on references more than text logprobs. If no head is specific, I'll stop this line and use the remaining passes to firm up the SC measurement on unused problems.
I picked two DEV reference solutions that reuse many numbers from their questions, 35 and 31 shared numbers. This pass reads their attention in the four full-attention layers on the original model.

The attention maps for both reference texts are in. For each operand in the response that also appears in the question, I'll find the query position that predicts its first digit, which is the token just before it. At that position, for each head, I'll measure the attention to the question occurrences of the same number. As a baseline I'll measure the same head's attention to all question digit tokens from text-predicting positions. A number-fetching head would show a high, specific match score.

Several full-attention heads attend specifically to the matching number in the question at the moment an operand is predicted, compared with their attention to question digits from ordinary text positions:

| Head | Match | Baseline | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| L5h2 | 0.171 | 0.014 | about 12x |
| L17h0 | 0.214 | 0.057 | about 4x |
| L11h1 | 0.131 | 0.034 | about 4x |
| L23h2 | 0.122 | 0.032 | about 4x |

These look like number-fetching heads. This is only correlational and rests on two texts, so I'll test causally. I'll zero the o_proj input columns of these four heads, as the only edit and with SC dropped (SC stays backed up in /work/best_SC). Then I'll score the same 1,024 screen texts as pass 3, which give the original baseline. If the heads carry operands from the question, operand-start logprobs on the 876 references should fall much more than text and result-digit logprobs. If all classes fall equally, the heads are generic and amplifying them would not target operand selection.
